body:
<!-- pr-reviewer: 5c1edd03f37fbac8d9d5834b45a09df015bd06d8 -->
Ready for the maintainer to merge.

The approach from the air is exact polygon geometry, not a strip of stock open by a
constant. The safety floor holds. I verified the negative pin is load-bearing by
mutation: with the area test removed from `link/approach.rs`, the pin
`an_approach_that_would_cut_stock_off_the_curve_is_refused` fails as expected
(the link stays through the tooth of stock beside the start, [(-20, 25), (-20, 29),
(20, 29), (20, 25)]). I reverted the mutation and re-ran the pin green.

**What looks good**
- The proof of the stretch is the swept disc, less the swath of the next piece
  (the disc swept along that piece, grown by the 10 um flattening tolerance), required
  to lie within the grown air. No constant strip.
- Every sample of the stretch is in the air or the edge band (clear of the part zone),
  more than a tool radius from each keep-out area, and not inside the cutter-centre
  area (within `ROOM_TOL` of its boundary, or near the start of the piece). The
  stretch holds in the legal room of the entry stage. It crosses no cut made, no link,
  and no planned cut away from the ends.
- The way out to the door reuses the three tries of K4 in one function (`proof::tries`).
  The approach is the fourth try, after the straight chord, the chain back-chord and the
  edge walk. The plan has no new step kind.
- `a_link_leaves_a_cut_at_the_stock_edge_runs_in_the_air_and_comes_back_over_cleared_stock`
  now stays as an approach; it was pinned as the old refusal. The record
  (`docs/decisions/4254-kernel-air-approach.md`) covers the area-test rule, the no-new-step
  decision, and the dropped alternatives (a new plan step, a tangent approach, an arc lead,
  a fourth try in the edge route only). Provenance line on the new module.
- The measured reading matches the body: the dog bone Outside carries one full-width feed
  at (-2.40, 25.00) on the top stock edge; the disc carries zero.

**Results** (trial merge against `origin/side/path-kernel` df9ec30: already up to date;
all ran locally in the review worktree, not the runner)
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/side/path-kernel`: 4 steps ok
  (pathkernel build, lib, laws; motion kernel_laws)
- `camcraft-pathkernel` laws: 140 passed
- `camcraft-motion` kernel_laws: 30 passed
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-pathkernel -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: ok
- `cargo xtask gate light --base origin/side/path-kernel`: 7 steps ok, 0 failed (light twins, release)

**Targeted checks (step 5)**
- No post or toolpath change: no example catalog suites were run (no planner calls the
  approach yet; the default planner output is identical).
- Light lane: 7 steps ok, not red.
- P2 (enhancement), not P1: no targeted heavy step owed.

**Pin verification (K3)**
- The changed k3_load rows in the PR head match the body's new numbers. The kernel_laws
  suite passes with them: disc Outside `None` 415/145/19; `constant 25 %` 344/122/81; dog
  bone Outside `None` 739/180/13; `constant 25 %` 683/143/69. Inside rows unchanged
  (disc 3507/173/0 and 833/173/1; dog bone 2587/173/0 and 581/173/1).
- The measured row prints (over 415 / worst 145 / full 0; over 739 / worst 180 / full 1)
  match the pins.

**Requested before merge**
None - the code is clean. The items below are notes, not blockers.

**Questions / notes (not blocking)**
1. Stack order with #4279 (same file): this PR and #4279 re-pin the same k3_load rows in
   `crates/motion/tests/kernel_laws/k3_load.rs`, and both touch
   `crates/motion/tests/kernel_laws/k4_order_link.rs`. Whichever of the two merges second
   must take `origin/side/path-kernel` and re-measure or reconcile. The rows are not
   directly comparable: #4279 re-pins the disc constant row to 337/118/77 with a different
   path builder (`cuts_path_with`, the cuts without the entry leads).
   The "before" rows cited in the body and in the `k3_load.rs` comment are the side head's
   committed pins (402/145/13, 334/118/74 on the disc; 724/167/3, 678/143/66 on the dog
   bone). Those were measured by #4265 against a base without #4253. The current side head
   reads 337/118/77 for the constant row. The after-values are consistent with that
   baseline (344 = 337 + 7; 81 = 77 + 4; 122 = 118 + 4). Worth citing 337/118/77 as the
   baseline in the comment and the PR body at merge time.
2. `Refs #4254` at the end of the body: the issue's done-means is met (0 lifts on the
   disc and the dog bone; pins green). `Fixes #4254` would be the natural close. Kept as a
   question, not a change request - `Refs` is fine if the issue stays open by design until
   the side branch merges.
3. The one full-width approach on the dog bone (at (-2.40, 25.00)) is acknowledged in
   the body with follow-up #4272 (the load stage does not read the approach). That
   follow-up is the right place for it.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
